clue.text: Latest form of harvest rotation?

parts.note: the clue pretends to be about farmers rotating crops, but means the flattened circular patterns that mysteriously appear in fields of grain

explanation.surface: A farming innovation: the newest system for rotating crops from season to season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotation' suggests the farming practice of changing crops field by field; here it is literal roundness, a circle pressed into a standing crop.
explanation.definitionFit: These flattened rings in wheat fields are a recent phenomenon, a whimsical 'form' made from the harvest that literally rotates.

clue.text: Area sounds uncultivated

indicators.note: the clue says the word for uncultivated is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: uncultivated in the sense of unrefined or coarse, that is rude

explanation.surface: A patch of land sounds as though it has never been farmed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is an old British unit of land area, a quarter of an acre; it also means a cross, which is not used here.
explanation.definitionFit: An old measure of land equal to a quarter acre, so it names an area.

clue.text: It's used to pound mortar

parts.note: mortar looks like the builder's cement, but here it is the bowl in which spices are ground by a club-shaped tool

explanation.surface: A builder's tool for working cement.
explanation.walkthrough: Mortar suggests bricklaying; the kitchen mortar is the bowl, and its partner is the tool that pounds in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The club-shaped grinding tool is paired with a mortar bowl for crushing herbs and spices.

clue.text: Accuse the little devil of taking every one

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
each means every one taken individually

explanation.surface: Someone blames the mischievous little devil for grabbing every single one.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a formal charge of misconduct against an official is to accuse them.

clue.text: First bit of lamb stuck in a tooth can make one choke

indicators.note: the letter is lodged inside the word for a tooth, as food sticks between teeth

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word lamb is used

explanation.surface: A shred of lamb caught between the teeth might make someone gag.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooth suggests a mouth, but the tooth here is a cog on a gearwheel; choke is used in its sense of block or obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To block up a pipe or passage is to choke it, as leaves obstruct a drain.

clue.text: Suffers and conclude certain changes are needed

indicators.note: says the letters of the two words just given must be altered in order to fit

parts.note: to conclude is to end
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with hardship and decides that some reforms must happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes are needed' rearranges ENDSURE, built from END and SURE, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear pain or hardship without giving way is to suffer it patiently.

clue.text: Don't turn to crime?

parts.note: read literally it is an instruction not to swerve, but idiomatically it means to live honestly after release from prison

explanation.surface: A warning to someone not to take up a criminal life.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both 'keep on without turning' and 'reform after a criminal past', which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an ex-offender living lawfully also literally means keep driving ahead without turning.

clue.text: Kissagram agency-an insincere profession?

definitions.meaning: a business sending kisses would offer service by the lips
a profession here is a declaration of belief, made in words only, without real commitment

explanation.surface: A firm sending kissing messengers is described as a dishonest line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Profession looks like a career, but means an avowal, as in a profession of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names support expressed in words but not backed by deeds, and jokingly a mouth-based delivery business.

clue.text: Note retreat of W African tribe to desert

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: a retreat goes backwards, so the tribe's name is read from end to start

parts.note: the Ibo (Igbo) are a people of south-eastern Nigeria

explanation.surface: A musical signal marks a West African people's withdrawal into the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: IBO reversed gives OBI.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast arid region spanning Mongolia and northern China, one of the world's great deserts.

clue.text: Audience standing up, well-pleased with one's address

parts.note: a theatre audience is the house, as in a full house
proud can mean projecting or sticking up above a surface

explanation.surface: An audience on its feet, delighted with the speech that has just been made.
explanation.walkthrough: Address suggests a speech, matching the standing audience; it really means one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes great pride in keeping their home tidy and attractive is pleased with where they live.

clue.text: Joins one in new tunes

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the rearranged letters
new tells us the letters of tunes are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone fits a single extra melody into a fresh set of tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TUNES into UNTES, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring things together into one whole is to join them, as a treaty brings nations together.

clue.text: Permit bad behaviour?

definitions.meaning: a permit is an official document granting permission, such as a driving or TV one
excessive freedom, disregard of rules, as in poetic or sexual excess

explanation.surface: A document allowing misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling with -ce is used for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an official authorisation and irresponsible freedom of conduct.

clue.text: Alibi tenor used to get release

indicators.note: used suggests the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A singer's excuse is employed to win his freedom from custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges ALIBI and TENOR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set free from confinement or oppression is a release.

clue.text: Happen to reach a gap in the hills

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
a mountain pass is a gap through hills

explanation.surface: Travellers manage to get to a gap in a hill range.
explanation.definitionFit: When events finally occur, they are said to come about or take place.

clue.text: Is paid pots, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word for pots is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: urns are large pots or vases

explanation.surface: Someone receives payment in pots, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match works in British speech, where the R is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who receives wages for work is gaining money.

clue.text: Aspired to be a literary giant

indicators.note: to be signals that the letters of aspired become something different

explanation.surface: Someone longed to become a great writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' rearranges ASPIRED. A literary giant suggests a great author, but this is Giant Despair, an ogre in Bunyan's 'The Pilgrim's Progress'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bunyan's allegory, the Giant of Doubting Castle bears this name, so he is a giant from literature.

clue.text: Put off Ted's rise with hesitation

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads upward, so the name is reversed

parts.note: the name Ted, possessive 's contributing no letters
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Ted's promotion is postponed because of doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns TED into DET.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to put them off.

clue.text: Where one would find a wandering shade?

definitions.text: Where one would find a wandering shade?

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of shade stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about where a roaming ghost would be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges SHADE; the whole clue also defines, since the dead wander as shades in the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the underworld is the realm where ghosts of the dead roam.

clue.text: Rustic's family deserts him-what a blow!.

indicators.note: the family leaves, so its letters are taken away from the word for a rustic

parts.note: a bumpkin is an unsophisticated country person
kin means family

explanation.surface: A country fellow's relations abandon him, and it is a terrible shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock or thump is a blow.

clue.text: Fruit said to be unpleasant

indicators.note: the clue says the word for unpleasant is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: ugly can mean unpleasant, as in an ugly mood

explanation.surface: A fruit with a reputation for being disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: This trademarked fruit is a Jamaican cross between grapefruit and tangerine, named for its wrinkly look.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus hybrid with a rough, wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Bury in Milan?

definitions.meaning: to bury a corpse is to place it in the grave
the football club based in Milan, known as Internazionale

explanation.surface: Laying someone to rest in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the English town (with its own football club); it is a verb. The second sense is Inter Milan, the football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to lay a body in a grave, and is the familiar name of a Milanese football club.

clue.text: Criminal gets Gill confused with ale

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker mixes up a measure of drink with beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges GILL and ALE together; a gill is a small British measure of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against the law is unlawful, which is what criminal means as an adjective.

clue.text: Rake money in, in the usual way

indicators.note: the money word goes inside the word for a rake

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roue
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone gathers in cash as normal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rake looks like a verb for gathering; it is a womaniser, ROUE, with TIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular established procedure is the customary way of doing things.

clue.text: Sells or tells

definitions.meaning: sells goods to the public in shops

explanation.surface: Someone sells or tells.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to sell goods to customers and to repeat or relate a story.

clue.text: It is worn as a favour

definitions.text: It is worn as a favour

parts.words: It is worn as a favour
parts.note: favour suggests a kindness, but here it is a badge of ribbon worn to show support or as a prize

explanation.surface: Something one puts on to oblige somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour is also a ribbon or badge worn as a token, such as party colours or a winner's prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular ribbon badge worn to show allegiance or awarded as a prize.

clue.text: Provide company car

definitions.meaning: to accompany someone for protection or as a partner
the Ford model of that name

explanation.surface: A firm supplies a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Escort was a popular family car in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to accompany someone and is also a Ford motor model.

clue.text: Spinner the first player on the French pitch

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word player is used

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A spin bowler is the first player on a French cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like a sports field; it is a verb meaning fall forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch forward is to fall over, overbalance.

clue.text: Blueprint for a tail-less aircraft

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the word for an aircraft, like a plane missing its tail

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: Designs for an aircraft without a tail section.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed design or scheme drawn up in advance.

clue.text: This bird's the reverse of other birds

indicators.note: the names of the other birds are read backwards

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots

explanation.surface: One seabird is the opposite of some others.
explanation.definitionFit: A large, predatory seabird that robs gulls of their catch.

clue.text: Wealth is about to give security for nursery story girl

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Wealth is about to give security for nursery story girl' (GOLDILOCKS). GOLD + LOCKS is clear, but nothing gives the I: 'is about' supplies no I as printed, and a search found no other text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Wealth is about to give security for nursery story girl

clue.text: Get out of position

parts.note: read as removing someone from a post, it means expelling or forcing them out

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move from where they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel or remove someone from office is to force them out.

clue.text: Only staged irregularly, but it's always in June

indicators.note: irregularly tells us the letters of the two words fall out of order

explanation.surface: A show performed only now and then yet fixed in midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges ONLY and STAGED; in the northern hemisphere the summer solstice falls around 21 June.
explanation.definitionFit: The summer solstice, with most daylight, is always in June in the northern hemisphere.
